subChunks.title: Authentication vs Authorisation

storyBeats.text: The gates of the Academy have two guardians. The first asks: who are you? The second asks: are you allowed here?

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Authentication without authorisation is a door with a lock but no keys. Authorisation without authentication is a VIP room with no guest list. You need both.

storyBeats.label: Role check simulation

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Implement checkAccess(String role, String resource): return "ALLOWED" if role is "ADMIN" for any resource, or role is "USER" for "public". Otherwise "DENIED".
guidedPractice.hint: ADMIN can access any resource. USER can only access "public". Otherwise return "DENIED".

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between authentication and authorisation. Give a real-world analogy for each.

questions.prompt: In Spring Security, which component is responsible for loading user data during authentication?
questions.explanation: UserDetailsService.loadUserByUsername() is called during authentication to fetch user credentials and roles.

questions.prompt: Authorisation can happen before authentication in a Spring Security filter chain.
questions.explanation: Authentication must establish who the user is before authorisation can check what they're allowed to do.

subChunks.title: JWT Filter & Stateless Security

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: The JWT filter is the Academy's enchanted gate — every request passes through it. It reads the signet ring, verifies the seal, and if valid, admits the wizard and marks their identity in the Security Context.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate token extraction: given a header string like "Bearer abc.def.ghi", extract the token part. Return null if the header doesn't start with "Bearer ".
guidedPractice.hint: Check for null first, then check startsWith("Bearer "), then return substring(7).

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the JWT authentication filter flow in Spring Security. What is SecurityContextHolder?

questions.prompt: Why does a stateless JWT-based API set SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS?
options: To prevent Spring from creating HTTP sessions — each request is self-contained
To improve performance by disabling the database
questions.answer: To prevent Spring from creating HTTP sessions — each request is self-contained
questions.explanation: Stateless means no server-side session. The JWT carries all authentication info, so no session store is needed.

subChunks.title: Method Security & OAuth2

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Method security is your finest-grained ward. The filter chain protects URLs. @PreAuthorize protects individual operations with SpEL expressions — the most powerful access control in Spring.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate @PreAuthorize: write deleteUser(String callerRole, Long userId) — only "ADMIN" can call it. Print "Deleted: " + userId or throw an IllegalStateException("Access denied").
guidedPractice.hint: If callerRole is not "ADMIN", throw new IllegalStateException("Access denied"). Otherwise print "Deleted: " + userId.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between @PreAuthorize and @PostAuthorize. When would you use each?

questions.prompt: What annotation enables method-level security in Spring?

subChunks.title: Password Encoding & CSRF

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Storing plain-text passwords is not just wrong — it's inexcusable. BCrypt turns a password into an irreversible hash with a built-in cost factor. Even if your database is stolen, passwords are safe.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate BCrypt's concept: write hashPassword(String raw) that returns "hashed:" + raw.length() + ":salt", and matches(String raw, String hash) that checks if the hash starts with "hashed:" + raw.length().
guidedPractice.hint: hashPassword returns "hashed:" + raw.length() + ":salt". matches checks hash.startsWith("hashed:" + raw.length()).

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Why is BCrypt preferred over MD5 or SHA-256 for password storage?

questions.prompt: Why should you never store plain-text passwords?
options: A database breach would expose all user passwords immediately
Plain text is slower to compare
questions.answer: A database breach would expose all user passwords immediately
questions.explanation: Hashing with BCrypt means a stolen database doesn't directly reveal passwords — attackers must brute-force each hash.
